NoCHF

NoCHF

This site outlines the purpose and development of the NoCHF app, a student capstone project to meet partial fulfillment of the requirements for a Master of Liberal Arts degree from Harvard University Extension School

NoCHF is an app that aims to reduce avoidable hospitalizations and emergency room visits for people living with congestive heart failure. The app:

  • Ensures daily blood pressure and weight measurements.
  • Alerts patients when their readings meet doctor-defined criteria for follow up with their professional care giver.
  • Provides a simple, easy-to-use phone app designed for older adults.

Understanding CHF

Congestive heart failure

Congestive heart failure (CHF) is heart failure accompanied by fluid buildup, often in the lungs, legs, ankles, or other tissues. Two common forms are HFrEF, in which the heart pumps weakly, and HFpEF, in which the heart is too stiff to fill properly.12 Advanced heart failure is a severe stage in which symptoms persist despite treatment and may occur even at rest. CHF can progress to this stage, but fluid buildup alone does not mean the disease is advanced.7

Daily monitoring is hard to sustain for CHF patients

Patients completed the full set of weight, blood pressure, heart-rate, and symptom readings on approximately 74% of days in a heart-failure monitoring study.
